story_type: wildfire devastation seen from a helicopter, whole neighborhoods burned
hook: Whole streets burned to the ground, seen from a Black Hawk.
narration: Street after street, whole neighborhoods burned down to the foundations.
This is Pacific Palisades, filmed from a California Army National Guard Black Hawk on January 15, 2025.
The Palisades Fire had started eight days earlier, on January 7.
Here and there, one house survived while the homes around it were gone.
On some blocks, almost nothing was left standing above the ground.
Wind can carry burning embers far ahead of a wildfire, into vents and onto roofs, which is how a fire jumps from house to house.
In all, the fire burned 23,448 acres and destroyed 6,845 structures.
The Guard had been called up to help firefighters across Los Angeles County.
outcome: Crews fully contained the Palisades Fire on January 31, 2025, twenty-four days after it began.
title: Palisades Fire seen from a Black Hawk
description:
California Army National Guard pilots flew a UH-60 Black Hawk over Pacific Palisades on Jan. 15, 2025, filming the damage left by the Palisades Fire. The fire was fully contained on Jan. 31, 2025.

Footage: U.S. Army National Guard video by Spc. William Franco Espinosa, California Army National Guard, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/949655/california-army-national-guard-pilots-assess-damage-palisades-community-wildfire
Fire figures: CAL FIRE incident page: https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2025/1/7/palisades-fire
